claude_take: Every story that depended on someone else's permission moved slowly today, and every story that didn't moved instantly. Nvidia's board closed the Jensen Huang chapter in one sentence and reported record profits in the next; Netflix is positioned to pick up a legendary studio lot for roughly a third of what its lenders first demanded. Meanwhile a Milan court postponed a child-safety case against Meta and TikTok until Italy's parliament finishes writing the law it's waiting on, and three nuclear-armed leaders held an unprecedented summit that produced mostly promises to keep talking. The tell is in the luxury numbers: European stocks with nothing to do with AI got dragged down anyway, purely on fear of a tech correction -- proof that capital's nerves now run through everything else's bloodstream.
claude_take_title: Capital Moves Fast. Everything Else Waits.

items.headline: Nvidia's Board Formally Rejects Jensen Huang's Return as CEO, Even as Profit Doubles
items.summary: Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones told investors the company has no plans to reinstate Jensen Huang after his abrupt resignation, calling it voluntary and final, even as Huang said he would be "honoured" to return. The announcement came alongside record results: $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue, up 103 percent year-over-year, with guidance of $130 billion for the current quarter. Huang is set to testify before Congress on December 1 over concerns that advanced US chips reached China, and the board is creating a new committee to oversee national-security and trade compliance.

items.headline: Google Quietly Makes Nano Banana 2.1 the Default Engine Behind Google Pics
items.summary: Google has rolled out Nano Banana 2.1, the latest version of its closely tracked image model, as the engine behind Google Pics' generation and editing tools for Google AI Pro, Plus and Ultra subscribers. The update keeps edits closer to the original image, makes fewer unrequested changes to surrounding elements, and improves text rendering in both new generations and edits. No user action is required: the model simply takes over behind the scenes in the standalone app and inside Google Docs and Slides.

items.headline: Netflix Positioned to Buy Radford Studio Center for a Third of What Lenders Wanted
items.summary: A foreclosure auction for the historic Radford Studio Center in Studio City is set for November 24, with lenders led by Goldman Sachs seeking $1.3 billion to cover their claim. Netflix, long under contract to buy the lot, is reportedly positioned to take it for roughly $400 million -- a steep discount secured by having Goldman foreclose rather than closing a conventional sale. The deal would hand Netflix a storied production hub at a fraction of its earlier valuation, underscoring how much distressed real estate is reshaping studio footprints right now.

items.headline: Gotham Awards Nominations Kick Off Hollywood's Awards Season, Led by Small Indies
items.summary: The 36th Gotham Awards nominations named "The Invite," "All of a Sudden," "Clarissa," "Possible Love" and "La Gradiva" among the films leading the field, chosen by juries of film professionals rather than a broad membership vote. The nominations formally open the run-up to the Oscars, with the ceremony set for November 30. Arriving the same week major studios keep absorbing each other into bigger conglomerates, the Gothams remain one of the few prizes built specifically to spotlight the kind of small, independent film that mergers tend to squeeze out.

items.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin Hold First-Ever Trilateral Summit on Nuclear Arms, Reach Only Modest Agreements
items.summary: On the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, Trump, Xi and Putin held an unprecedented three-way meeting with nuclear arms control at the center of the agenda -- the first leader-level talks on the subject since the New START treaty expired. Xi argued publicly that nuclear weapons should be "prohibited" and "eliminated," while the concrete outcomes were limited to modest commitments on UN reform, fuel supplies and continued dialogue. The summit's mere existence, bringing together three nuclear-armed rivals in this format for the first time, matters more than what it actually produced.

items.headline: Milan Court Delays Meta and TikTok Child-Safety Case Until Italy Finishes Writing a Law
items.summary: A Milan court postponed its ruling in a class action brought by the Italian parents' group Moige against Meta and TikTok over weak age-verification for users under 14, pushing the decision to January 21, 2027. The judges want to wait for Italy's parliament to finish a planned decree barring children under 13 from holding social media accounts before ruling. Parents involved in the case said their children remain exposed to the platforms in the meantime, a stark illustration of how far behind legislation is lagging platform design.

items.headline: European Luxury Stocks Slide as Fears of an AI Correction Spread to the Wealthy
items.summary: Shares in Hermès, Kering, Burberry and LVMH fell between roughly 2 and 4 percent as investors worried that a renewed selloff in AI stocks could cool the US wealth creation that has been propping up luxury spending while Chinese demand stays weak. Morgan Stanley has rated the sector "underweight" heading into 2027, even while noting the houses have little direct exposure to AI itself. The drop shows how tightly luxury's fortunes are now tied to a tech rally that has nothing to do with handbags or watches.

items.headline: Brain Scans Show Children With ADHD Have Lower Iron Levels in Specific Regions
items.summary: Presenting at the Society for Neuroscience's Neuroscience 2026 meeting, researcher Jonathan Ahern of UC San Diego reported that children and adolescents with ADHD show lower iron levels than neurotypical peers in specific brain regions, with the pattern shifting across different regions over time. Iron is a cofactor for the enzyme that helps produce dopamine, which has made it a longstanding target of interest in ADHD research, though earlier studies on the question have produced mixed results. The findings add to a broader set of results presented at the same meeting on how ADHD affects mental and physical health across the lifespan.

items.headline: Machiavelli's Virtù and Fortuna
items.headline_fr: La Virtù et la Fortuna de Machiavel
items.summary: Niccolò Machiavelli argued that political success depends on the interplay between virtù -- a ruler's skill, foresight and willingness to act decisively -- and fortuna, the unpredictable force of chance and circumstance that no amount of preparation can fully master. In The Prince, he likened fortune to a river that floods without warning, arguing the wise ruler builds dikes and levees in calm times rather than being caught unprepared. The idea still shapes how we think about leadership and risk: skill cannot guarantee outcomes, but unpreparedness guarantees failure when chance turns against you.
items.summary_fr: Nicolas Machiavel soutient que la réussite politique dépend de la tension entre la virtù -- l'habileté, la lucidité et la capacité d'un dirigeant à agir avec décision -- et la fortuna, cette part imprévisible du hasard et des circonstances qu'aucune préparation ne peut totalement maîtriser. Dans Le Prince, il compare la fortune à un fleuve qui déborde sans prévenir, estimant que le dirigeant avisé construit des digues par temps calme plutôt que de se laisser surprendre. Cette idée façonne encore notre manière de penser le pouvoir et le risque : l'habileté ne garantit jamais le résultat, mais l'impréparation garantit l'échec quand le hasard se retourne contre nous.
